tasks.title: Open an interactive shell
tasks.instructions:
Open an interactive shell inside the `web` container:

```bash
lxc shell web
```

Inside the container, run:
```bash
free -m
nproc
```

You should see 256 MiB of memory and 1 CPU (the limits set in the previous lab). Type `exit` to leave the shell.
hints: Your prompt will change to indicate you're inside the container.
Type 'exit' to return to your host terminal.
tasks.solution:
```bash
lxc shell web
# Inside:
free -m
nproc
exit
```

tasks.title: Run a single command with exec
tasks.instructions:
Use `lxc exec` to run a command inside the `web` container without opening a shell:

```bash
lxc exec web -- cat /etc/os-release
```

This shows the OS version running inside the container.
hints: The -- separator prevents lxc from interpreting command flags.
lxc exec runs one command and returns the output to your host terminal.

tasks.title: Install a package inside the container
tasks.instructions:
Use `lxc exec` to install a package inside the `web` container:

```bash
lxc exec web -- apt update
lxc exec web -- apt install -y nginx
```

Then verify nginx is installed:
```bash
lxc exec web -- nginx -v
```
hints: apt update refreshes the package list. apt install -y installs without prompting.
tasks.solution:
```bash
lxc exec web -- apt update
lxc exec web -- apt install -y nginx
lxc exec web -- nginx -v
```
